title: Sold-item 'returned' basis bypasses sale-proceeds reversal (economic dupe loop)
description:
Post-merge review of PR #455 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19).

## Defect

A sold inventory row can be restored payment-free via `basis: 'returned'`, leaving the character with both the item and the sale proceeds — the exact economic dupe loop the repurchase-payment work was built to close.

Code facts (all verified):

- `packages/core/src/state/domainMutations.ts` `reacquireItem`: the disposition/basis compatibility gate (~line 667) rejects only `sold+found` and `lost+repurchased`; `sold+returned` passes.
- Payment is *required* for `repurchased` and *forbidden* for `found`/`returned` (~lines 628-635), so the `returned` path performs no wallet mutation by construction.
- Schema agrees: `inventory_custody_event` CHECK `(basis='repurchased') = (payment_event_id IS NOT NULL)` (migration 0018).
- Existing tests pin the payment-free sold-item return ("The merchant rescinded the sale and handed it back") as passing behavior.

Loop: sell item → keep proceeds → narrate a return → `reacquire_item { basis: 'returned' }` → item + proceeds retained. In gameplay the DM model adjudicates the evidence string, so a player steering the narration is enough; there is no deterministic economic backstop on this path, unlike every other transition in this family.

## Fix direction (per review recommendation)

- Make `returned` valid only for `lost` rows (extend the compatibility gate).
- For sold rows, require either `repurchased` (existing atomic payment) or a new `sale-reversed` basis that atomically reverses the original sale proceeds (credit debit mirroring the sale wallet event).
- A genuinely gratuitous merchant gift-back, if it must be supported, should be its own explicit basis with a deliberate decision — not the default free path.

Note: adding a payment-carrying basis (`sale-reversed`) conflicts with the immutable migration-0018 CHECK `(basis='repurchased') = (payment_event_id IS NOT NULL)` on `inventory_custody_event`, so a new migration is required to widen that constraint (and the basis enum CHECK). Update `toolReacquireItem.ts` schema/description, `listRecoverableItems` basis filtering (`domainMutations.ts` ~line 440-463), and the tests that currently pin the payment-free sold-return.

Related: eshyra follow-ups from the same review — migration-0018 oversized-stack unresolvable edge, and the numeric-conservation dice-modifier gate.
